title: What Satellite Photos of Penguin Poop Tell Us About Earth’s Health
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentWhat Satellite Photos of Penguin Poop Tell Us About Earth’s HealthClimate change is painting with an Adélie penguin palette on Antarctic ice floesDRBy Devin Reese11:00 AM CDT on July 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GooglePenguin poo, or guano, is a popular resource. Nests for penguin eggs are bowl-shaped depressions that the parents hollow into piles of guano and soil. And farmers love penguin guano for its rich nutrients, particularly nitrogen. In fact, guano harvest for farm fertilizer during the 19th century forced penguins to lay so many eggs on exposed ground that it led to population crashes. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 00:00/00:561069.2K 20Climate Change Can Cause Birds to Alter Their Behavior in the Wrong DirectionShareNextStayNow, it turns out that guano is also useful for monitoring penguin recovery and responses to modern threats, as a recent study published in Current Biology used guano patterns to decipher how global climate change is affecting penguins. “It’s exactly what it sounds like,” explained study author Michael Polito, a marine biologist at the University of California, Santa Cruz, in a press release. “We spied on penguins from space by using satellite images to figure out what they eat all around Antarctica to help explain their diet and population response to recent climate change.”Already have an account?Log inJoin to continue readingYou've run out of free articles.
